title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two issues in `routing.py`:

1. Cache the generated request handler for effective route contexts to avoid rebuilding it on every request.
2. Replace the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with a `WeakKeyDictionary` to avoid stale cache entries and allow unused entries to be garbage-collected.

## Motivation

While reviewing `routing.py`, I noticed that routes using an effective route context rebuild their request handler on every incoming request, even though the effective context itself is already cached and stable. Caching the generated ASGI application avoids repeating the same work and reduces unnecessary allocations.

I also noticed that `_endpoint_context_cache` is keyed by `id(func)`. Since object IDs may be reused after an object is garbage-collected, this can theoretically return stale endpoint metadata. Additionally, the cache never shrinks because entries remain for the lifetime of the process. Using `WeakKeyDictionary` avoids both issues.

## Changes

- Added lazy caching of the generated ASGI application on `_EffectiveRouteContext`.
- Reused the cached application for subsequent requests.
- Replaced the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`.
- Added a fallback for callables that cannot be weak-referenced by computing the context without caching.

## Expected Impact

- Reduces repeated request handler construction.
- Avoids unnecessary allocations on repeated requests.
- Eliminates potential stale cache lookups caused by `id()` reuse.
- Prevents unbounded growth of the endpoint context cache.
- Preserves existing behavior while improving efficiency.

## Related Discussion

Related to: #discussion-10445342

## Testing

- Added tests covering the new behavior.
- Verified that the existing test suite passes.
- Confirmed that routing behavior remains unchanged while exercising the modified code paths.

title: Fix broken relative links in translated docs
body:
I noticed while looking at the translated documentation that there are three relative links that point to pages that are only in English. This results in 404s for users visiting the docs in any other locale than English.

What's broken
Affected files and links are:

docs//docs/deployment/versions.md — links to ../release-notes.md, which doesn't exist in any translated locale
docs//docs/help-fastapi.md — links to newsletter.md and fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts, which are not translated.
This impacts all 12 locales that are translated (de, es, fr, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant).

What I changed
Replaced broken relative links with absolute links to the English pages:

Old = ../release-notes.md
mew = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/

old = newsletter.md
new = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/newsletter/

old = fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts
new = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/fastapi-people/#fastapi-experts

Why absolute URLs
These pages (release-notes, newsletter, fastapi-people) are only maintained in English. It's a good idea to use absolute URLs here, as they will not silently fail if the page is renamed, and they will properly redirect translated users to the English version of the page, instead of a broken link. This is in line with other untranslated cross-references in the docs.

title: fix: pass include/exclude/by_alias params to jsonable_encoder when no response_model
body:
## Summary

`serialize_response` receives `include`, `exclude`, `by_alias`, `exclude_unset`, `exclude_defaults`, and `exclude_none` parameters. When `field` is None (no `response_model`), it calls `jsonable_encoder(response_content)` without passing any of those filtering parameters. They are silently ignored.

A user who writes `@app.get("/items", response_model_include={"name", "id"})` without a `response_model` would expect the exclude to work, but it doesn't.

## Verification
- Not dead code: called on every non-streaming endpoint response when no response_model is set.
- All existing tests pair `response_model_include`/`response_model_exclude` with `response_model`.

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
body:
Hi — thanks for FastAPI.

I noticed the published wheels lost their signed provenance in the switch to `uv`, and I don't think it was intended. Checking PyPI's integrity API:

| version | uploaded | `/integrity/.../provenance` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.127.0 | 2025-12-21 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| 0.128.0 | 2025-12-27 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| **0.129.0** | 2026-02-12 | **HTTP 404 — none** |
| 0.139.0 (latest) | 2026-07-01 | HTTP 404 — none |

The first release without provenance is the first one after `⬆️ Migrate to uv (#14676)`. That commit replaced `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (which emits PEP 740 attestations by default for Trusted Publishing projects) with `uv publish`, and uv's docs note it *"does not currently generate attestations."* The Trusted Publishing identity (`id-token: write`) is still configured, so it looks like only the emission step was dropped, silently — nothing fails in CI when attestations stop being produced, which is probably why it went unnoticed.

This PR keeps `uv build` and hands the upload back to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, which restores attestation emission. It's the one step, nothing else changes.

For a quick sanity check that the action still attests under Trusted Publishing: `huggingface/transformers` publishes this way and its wheels carry provenance today (`https://pypi.org/integrity/transformers/5.13.1/transformers-5.13.1-py3-none-any.whl/provenance` → 200).

I may be missing a reason `uv publish` was preferred here — if so, please just close this, no problem at all. If you'd rather keep `uv publish` and generate the attestations separately before upload, that works too; happy to adjust.

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
body:
Fixes #15974. Also reported in discussion #15914.

## Problem

`_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` rebuild their cached lists lazily with no synchronization. The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute before filling it and stamps the version afterwards. When several threads send the app's first requests concurrently (per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any setup that serves one app object from multiple event loops), multiple threads pass the version check and append into the same list. The cache ends up permanently holding duplicated candidates (around 600 entries for a 120 route app in the repro), a concurrent reader can see a partially built list and 404 a valid route, and the interleaved `warnings.catch_warnings()` calls inside the rebuild can leak global warnings filters.

## Fix

Guard the rebuild with a per-instance lock and double-checked version test, build the new list into a local variable, and publish it atomically (list first, version second). Readers on the fast path never see a partial list, concurrent first requests trigger exactly one rebuild, and the warnings filter state is no longer touched by interleaved rebuilds of the same router.

The lock field is excluded from the dataclass `repr` and `eq` so existing semantics are unchanged.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_included_router_concurrent_rebuild.py`, which fires the first requests from several threads through a barrier and asserts that all requests succeed and that the cache holds exactly one candidate per route. It fails on master and passes with this change. All existing router and include tests pass.

## Description

`contextmanager_in_threadpool` in `fastapi/concurrency.py` wraps a sync
context manager so its `__enter__`/`__exit__` run in a threadpool without
blocking the event loop. It is used for sync generator dependencies on async
endpoints (`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`).

The function manually reimplements `with`-statement semantics (enter,

The suite is split in two parts:

observable through the public API (FastAPI error middleware converts the
endpoint exception to a 500 before the dependency teardown suppression

- `__exit__` returning `True` suppresses the body exception
- `__exit__` returning `False` or `None` re-raises it

title: 🐛 Log ResponseValidationError from streaming endpoint serializers
body:
﻿When a streaming endpoint (SSE or JSONL) yields an item that fails response_model validation, FastAPI raises ResponseValidationError inside the streaming iterator. Currently that error is silently swallowed: no log entry is produced and the client receives an empty 200 OK that is indistinguishable from a valid zero-item stream.

Minimal reproduction:

```python
from collections.abc import AsyncIterable
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import EventSourceResponse
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Item(BaseModel):
    id: int

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/events", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
async def events() -> AsyncIterable[Item]:
    yield {"id": "NOT_AN_INT"}   # ResponseValidationError

r = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False).get("/events")
assert r.status_code == 200 and r.content == b""
# No log, no 500, no way to detect the error in production
```

Fix: catch ResponseValidationError in _producer (SSE), _async_stream_jsonl, and _sync_stream_jsonl, call logger.exception() to emit an ERROR-level log with full traceback (matching behavior for non-streaming endpoints), then re-raise so the exception continues to propagate. Valid streams are unaffected; the only change is that the error becomes visible.

This is distinct from fixing exceptions before the first yield (a design question around keepalive timing). This is exclusively about serialization errors on already-yielded items, where no such tension exists.

Adds 10 tests covering async and sync generator variants for both SSE and JSONL, verifying: ERROR log is emitted with exc_info, exception still propagates, valid streams produce no spurious logs.

Checks:

- `python -m pytest tests/test_stream_response_validation_error.py`
- `.\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe check fastapi/routing.py tests/test_stream_response_validation_error.py`
- `.\.venv\Scripts\ruff.exe format --check fastapi/routing.py tests/test_stream_response_validation_error.py`

title: ✨ Add QUERY HTTP method support to FastAPI
body:
## Description

This PR introduces a new custom HTTP method called **QUERY** to FastAPI for structured query operations.

The QUERY method follows the same pattern as existing HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and provides:
- Full integration with FastAPI's routing system
- Availability on both FastAPI and APIRouter classes
- Complete feature parity with other HTTP methods
- OpenAPI documentation support
- Response model validation

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14517

## Description

This PR adds support for [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) (Problem Details for HTTP APIs), which defines a standard machine-readable format for HTTP error responses using `Content-Type: application/problem+json`.

### Changes

- **`ProblemDetailsResponse`** (`fastapi/responses.py`) — new `JSONResponse` subclass with `media_type = "application/problem+json"`
- **`ProblemDetails` model** (`fastapi/problem_details.py`) — Pydantic model with `extra="allow"` for extension members
- **Type resolution** (`resolve_problem_type`) — 4-step hierarchy: explicit `type` > `problem_types` mapping > `error_kind` > auto-derivation from reason phrase (when `type_base_uri` set) > `about:blank` fallback
- **Exception handlers** (`fastapi/exception_handlers.py`) — reads config from `request.app` at runtime
- **`FastAPI.__init__`** (`fastapi/applications.py`) — new params: `problem_details`, `problem_type_base_uri`, `problem_types`
- **`HTTPException`** (`fastapi/exceptions.py`) — optional `type` param for per-exception override
- **OpenAPI schema** (`fastapi/openapi/utils.py`) — 422 responses use `application/problem+json` with `ProblemDetails` schema when enabled, including `additionalProperties: true`
- **31 tests** (`tests/test_problem_details.py`)

### Design decisions vs. discussion #14517

| Proposal | This PR | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `rfc9457=True` | `problem_details=True` | Matches RFC's own terminology; not tied to a spec number |
| Separate `ProblemDetailsException` | Extended `HTTPException` with `type` param | Less API surface, no new exception to learn |
| Per-router/per-route opt-in | App-level only | Exception handlers are global; per-route support requires threading through internals — best as a follow-up |

### Backward compatibility

Fully maintained — opt-in via `FastAPI(problem_details=True)`. Default behavior (`problem_details=False`) is unchanged.

title: fix(sse): emit data field for empty SSE data payload
body:
## What's broken
`format_sse_event()` drops the `data:` field entirely when the data payload is an empty string. It builds data lines via `data_str.splitlines()`, and `"".splitlines()` returns `[]`, so the loop never runs. Yielding `ServerSentEvent(raw_data="")` from an SSE endpoint produces a malformed event with no `data:` line and a single `\n` instead of the documented `\n\n` terminator, so clients can't recognize it as a discrete event.

```python
format_sse_event(data_str="")   # before: b'\n'   (expected b'data: \n\n')
```

## Why it happens
`str.splitlines()` returns `[]` for `""`, conflating an empty-but-present data payload with the "no data" (`None`) case, even though they're distinct.

## Fix
Emit a single empty `data:` line when the payload is the empty string (`data_str.splitlines() or [""]`), leaving the `None` case untouched.

## Test
Added `test_format_sse_event_empty_data_str` asserting `format_sse_event(data_str="") == b"data: \n\n"`. Fails before, passes after; full SSE suite (25) green.
